abstract: We investigate the graph isomorphism (GI) in some cospectral networks. Two graph are isomorphic when they are related to each other by a relabeling of the graph vertices. We want to investigate the GI in two scalable (n + 2)-regular graphs $G_{4}(n;n+2)$ and $G_{5}(n;n+2)$, analytically by using the multiparticle quantum walk. These two graphs are a pair of non-isomorphic connected cospectral regular graphs for any positive integer $n$. In order to investigation GI in these two graphs, we rewrite the adjacency matrices of graphs in the antisymmetric fermionic basis and show that they are different for these pairs of graphs. So the multiparticle quantum walk is able to distinguish pairs of non-isomorph graphs. Also we construct two new graphs $T_{4}(n;n+2)$ and $T_{5}(n;n+2)$ and repeat the same process of $G_{4}$ and $G_{5}$ to study the GI problem by using multiparticle quantum walk. Then we study GI by using the entanglement entropy. To this aim, we calculate entanglement entropy between two parts of network. In our model the nodes are considered as identical quantum harmonic oscillators. The entanglement entropy between two special parts of $G_{4}(n;n+2)$ and $G_{5}(n;n+2)$ are calculated analytically. It is shown that the entanglement entropy can distinguish pairs of non-isomorphic cospectral graphs too.

specification.problem: Decide whether two given connected (n+2)-regular cospectral graphs, G_4(n;n+2) and G_5(n;n+2) (and the related T_4, T_5), are non-isomorphic by (i) comparing their adjacency operators rewritten in the antisymmetric (fermionic) multiparticle basis of a continuous-time quantum walk and (ii) comparing ground-state entanglement entropies of harmonic-oscillator networks defined on the graphs.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scoped to ONE construction: a two-fermion (antisymmetric two-particle) continuous-time quantum walk generated by the graph adjacency matrix, applied to a pair of N-vertex k-regular cospectral graphs with adjacency matrices A and A', with the smallest parameter n=1 (k=3) as the nominal tiny instance. The explicit vertex sets/edge sets of G_4(n;n+2), G_5(n;n+2), T_4, T_5 are not given in the abstract and are left as missing inputs. The harmonic-oscillator entanglement-entropy test is given only as a standard Gaussian-state background formula with an assumed coupling matrix; its specific bipartition ('two special parts') and the analytic closed-form entropies of the paper remain outside scope. Walks with more than two particles, the T_4/T_5 constructions, and the paper's analytic proofs are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: The two graphs of a cospectral pair (e.g. G_4(n;n+2) and G_5(n;n+2))
symbols.domain: simple connected k-regular graphs on N vertices, k=n+2

symbols.meaning: Number of vertices of each graph
symbols.domain: positive integer (unknown function of n for G_4, G_5)

symbols.meaning: Adjacency matrices of G and G' (vertices labelled 0..N-1)
symbols.domain: symmetric 0/1 matrices in \{0,1\}^{N\times N}, zero diagonal, row sums k

symbols.meaning: Permutation matrix implementing a vertex relabeling
Antisymmetric (two-fermion) basis state with particles on vertices i<j
symbols.domain: orthonormal basis of the \binom{N}{2}-dimensional antisymmetric subspace of \mathbb{C}^N\otimes\mathbb{C}^N

symbols.meaning: Adjacency (walk) operator rewritten in the antisymmetric fermionic basis
Potential (coupling) matrix of the harmonic-oscillator network
symbols.domain: real symmetric positive-definite N\times N matrix

symbols.meaning: Von Neumann entanglement entropy of the oscillator subset \mathcal A in the network ground state
Symplectic eigenvalues of the reduced covariance matrix of subset \mathcal A

equations.label: Graph isomorphism as vertex relabeling
equations.latex: G \cong G' \iff \exists P \in S_N:\; A' = P A P^{T}
equations.description: Two graphs are isomorphic iff their adjacency matrices are related by simultaneous row/column permutation.
equations.abstract_quote: Two graph are isomorphic when they are related to each other by a relabeling of the graph vertices.
equations.justification: Direct matrix statement of the relabeling definition given in the abstract.
assumptions: Vertices labelled 0..N-1 so that A is an N x N matrix.

equations.label: Cospectrality of the non-isomorphic pair
equations.latex: \det(\lambda I - A) = \det(\lambda I - A') \;\forall \lambda \quad\text{while}\quad \nexists P:\; A' = P A P^{T}
equations.description: The pair has identical adjacency spectra (so single-particle quantum walks have identical energy spectra) yet is non-isomorphic.
equations.abstract_quote: These two graphs are a pair of non-isomorphic connected cospectral regular graphs for any positive integer $n$.
equations.justification: 'Cospectral' is standardly taken with respect to the adjacency matrix; the abstract asserts both cospectrality and non-isomorphism.
assumptions: Cospectrality refers to the adjacency spectrum (not Laplacian), consistent with the adjacency-based walk used in the paper.

equations.label: Adjacency in the antisymmetric two-fermion basis
equations.latex: |ij\rangle_- = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\big(|i\rangle|j\rangle - |j\rangle|i\rangle\big),\; i<j;\qquad A^{(2)}_{(ij),(kl)} = {}_-\langle ij|\,(A\otimes I + I\otimes A)\,|kl\rangle_- = \delta_{jl}A_{ik} + \delta_{ik}A_{jl} - \delta_{jk}A_{il} - \delta_{il}A_{jk}
equations.description: Matrix elements of the two-particle hopping operator restricted to the antisymmetric (fermionic) subspace; this is the smallest multiparticle version of 'rewriting the adjacency matrix in the antisymmetric fermionic basis'.
equations.abstract_quote: we rewrite the adjacency matrices of graphs in the antisymmetric fermionic basis
equations.justification: The abstract names the antisymmetric fermionic basis; the explicit two-particle, non-interacting form is the minimal standard realisation. The paper may use more particles or additional terms.
assumptions: Exactly two particles (smallest nontrivial multiparticle case).
Non-interacting particles: the two-particle generator is A⊗I + I⊗A with no interaction term.

equations.label: Two-fermion continuous-time walk and its spectrum
equations.latex: U^{(2)}(t) = e^{-i t A^{(2)}},\qquad p_t(kl\,|\,ij) = \big|{}_-\langle kl|U^{(2)}(t)|ij\rangle_-\big|^2,\qquad \mathrm{spec}\big(A^{(2)}\big) = \{\lambda_a+\lambda_b : a<b\}
equations.description: Walk unitary generated by the antisymmetric-basis adjacency and the resulting pair-occupation distribution. For non-interacting fermions the two-particle spectrum is determined by the single-particle spectrum, so cospectral pairs (eq_2) yield identical two-particle spectra; any distinguishing power must come from comparing the matrices/dynamics beyond the spectrum, as the paper's criterion (not stated in the abstract) presumably does.
equations.justification: Standard continuous-time quantum walk definition and the standard spectral decomposition of a non-interacting two-particle Hamiltonian on the antisymmetric subspace.
assumptions: Hamiltonian is the adjacency matrix (not the Laplacian) with unit hopping and \hbar=1.
Non-interacting two-fermion model as in eq_3.

equations.label: Harmonic-oscillator network ground state (assumed coupling)
equations.latex: H_{\mathrm{osc}} = \tfrac12\sum_{i} p_i^2 + \tfrac12\, x^{T} K x,\quad K = \omega_0^2 I + L,\; L = kI - A;\qquad \Sigma_x = \tfrac12 K^{-1/2},\; \Sigma_p = \tfrac12 K^{1/2}
equations.description: Nodes as identical unit-mass quantum harmonic oscillators coupled along edges; the ground state is Gaussian with position/momentum covariance matrices fixed by K.
equations.justification: The abstract states nodes are identical harmonic oscillators but does not give the coupling matrix; the Laplacian coupling with an on-site frequency \omega_0>0 (to make K positive definite) is a common choice and is proposed here as an explicit assumption.
assumptions: Coupling matrix K = \omega_0^2 I + L with \omega_0 > 0; the paper's actual K (e.g. adjacency-based or different normalisation) is unknown.

equations.label: Entanglement entropy of a node subset from symplectic eigenvalues
equations.description: Von Neumann entropy of the reduced Gaussian state of oscillator subset \mathcal A (one 'part' of the network); the GI test compares S_{\mathcal A}(G) with S_{\mathcal A'}(G') for corresponding parts.
equations.justification: Standard formula for the entropy of a Gaussian state in terms of symplectic eigenvalues of the reduced covariance matrix; the abstract says entropy between two parts of the network is computed but does not specify the parts or the closed form.
assumptions: Pure Gaussian ground state so that S of one part equals the entanglement entropy of the bipartition.
Choice of subset \mathcal A ('two special parts') unspecified by the abstract.

registers.name: v1
registers.role: Vertex position of fermion 1 (integer i encoded in binary, qubit 0 = least significant bit)

registers.name: v2
registers.role: Vertex position of fermion 2 (integer j encoded in binary, qubit 0 = least significant bit)

specification.initial_state: |\psi_0\rangle = |i_0 j_0\rangle_- = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}(|i_0\rangle_{v1}|j_0\rangle_{v2} - |j_0\rangle_{v1}|i_0\rangle_{v2}) for a chosen adjacent or fixed vertex pair i_0<j_0 (same labels used for both graphs); the choice of (i_0,j_0) is an assumption.

steps.description: Classically build A and A' for the pair (G,G') and form the antisymmetric-basis operators A^{(2)} and A'^{(2)} (eq_3); verify cospectrality of A and A' (eq_2) so that single-particle spectra cannot distinguish them.
Prepare the antisymmetric two-particle initial state |i_0 j_0\rangle_- on registers v1,v2.
For each graph, apply the two-fermion walk unitary U^{(2)}(t) = exp(-i t A^{(2)}) (Hamiltonian simulation of A⊗I + I⊗A, which preserves the antisymmetric subspace) for one or more times t.

Measure v1,v2 in the computational basis to estimate the pair-occupation distribution p_t(kl|i_0 j_0) for each graph; compare the two distributions (and/or the matrices A^{(2)}, A'^{(2)} directly) as the GI witness.

(Classical, outside the quantum circuit) Build the oscillator coupling K for each graph, compute reduced covariance matrices of the chosen subset \mathcal A, and compare entanglement entropies S_{\mathcal A}(G) vs S_{\mathcal A'}(G').

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of registers v1 and v2 after U^{(2)}(t), giving vertex pairs (k,l); outcomes with k=l have zero probability for an ideal antisymmetric state. Repeat to estimate p_t(kl|i_0 j_0) for each graph.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compare the estimated distributions p_t(·|i_0 j_0) for G and G' (e.g. total-variation distance over all choices of initial pair and times used); report 'non-isomorphic' if they differ beyond statistical error for some (i_0,j_0,t) under a fixed labelling convention, noting that the abstract's actual comparison criterion ('adjacency matrices ... are different') is not specified. Separately, compute S_{\mathcal A} from eq_5–eq_6 for each graph and compare.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the smallest construction chosen is a two-fermion non-interacting continuous-time walk generated by the adjacency matrix, with nominal tiny instance n=1 (3-regular G_4(1;3), G_5(1;3)).
Two particles only; the paper's 'multiparticle' walk may use more particles.
Hamiltonian = adjacency matrix with unit hopping, \hbar=1.
Oscillator coupling matrix taken as K = \omega_0^2 I + L with \omega_0>0 (eq_5); the paper's actual oscillator Hamiltonian is unknown.
Initial vertex pair (i_0,j_0) and the entropy bipartition \mathcal A are free choices not fixed by the abstract.

Caveat: for non-interacting fermions, spec(A^{(2)}) is fixed by spec(A), so cospectral graphs give isospectral two-fermion walks; distinguishing them requires comparing the full operators/dynamics, not spectra.
missing_information: Explicit vertex and edge sets (or construction rule) of G_4(n;n+2), G_5(n;n+2), T_4(n;n+2), T_5(n;n+2), including N as a function of n.
Number of particles used in the paper's multiparticle walk and whether any interaction term is included.
The precise criterion by which the antisymmetric-basis adjacency matrices are declared 'different' (a non-isomorphism invariant beyond the spectrum).
The harmonic-oscillator network Hamiltonian (coupling matrix, on-site frequency, normalisation).
Definition of the 'two special parts' (bipartition) used for the entanglement entropy and the analytic entropy expressions.
Any proof or argument that the invariants are robust across all positive integers n.
